summary: The split-completion, one-orientation and weighted extension-pair arguments withstand direct degenerate-case analysis. Equal coordinate edges and singleton coordinate intersections each produce a valid third star member distinct from both residual completions. The concentration argument requires no injectivity of the extension-pair map and no uniqueness of the heavy point. A supplementary exact check on the inherited six-point design found no counterexample.

findings.statement: All coordinate intersection sizes 0, 1 and 2 are covered; in the equal-edge case the design block obtained by restoring the anchor has exactly the shared edge as trace on both completions.
findings.disposition: No missing equal-projection or distinctness case was found.

findings.statement: The heavy extension-pair argument does not need distinct keys to have distinct extension pairs. Its final injection is Q to Q union {a}, with a outside every key Q.
findings.disposition: The manuscript correctly avoids claiming a canonical extension-pair permutation check as a premise.

checks.scope: Split completion compatibility, including degenerate cases
checks.method: Directly analyzed each possible intersection cardinality of two two-element coordinate edges and compared with CompletionCompatibility.lean. Ran scratch/domain_expert/round03_check.py over all 36 anchor pairs and 10,800 unordered pairs of the 25 coordinate completions.
checks.observation: When one coordinate is disjoint, the other coordinate has size-0, size-1 or size-2 intersection. The first gives an empty-core sunflower with R; the latter two give a star-member witness. The star includes x, which no completion contains, so all three sets are distinct. Of the tested pairs, 7,200 have a disjoint coordinate (1,800 empty, 3,600 singleton, 1,800 equal cases), and every one has a directly verified sunflower witness. This finite check concerns the explicit design only; the abstract trace proof provides the general argument.

checks.scope: One orientation and unique block extensions
checks.method: Checked disjoint completion type cardinalities and distinctness of the three members used to bound W; tested the nonempty-row and duplicate-key cases in the proof.
checks.observation: A row supported on two A points needs nine distinct (1,3) completions, while a B-oriented row needs nine distinct (3,1) completions. The types are disjoint and cannot both fit into n0 at most 12. Since n2 is at least 24, an orientation exists. Two extensions of a single B triple, with different A points, and its x-star member are three distinct sets with exactly that triple as common intersection; hence W has at most ten members.

checks.scope: Common-extension concentration and fixed-key fiber bound
checks.method: Proved the heavy-point implication directly from 9-unit pair weight and 10-unit total, checked the key-to-block injection, and enumerated all 8,008 six-point nonnegative integer weight vectors of total at most ten in scratch/domain_expert/round03_check.py.
checks.observation: A selected heavy pair has a point of weight at least five. Any heavy pair omitting it would give at least 14 total units, contradiction. Equal extension pairs and multiple high-weight points do not invalidate this argument. The common point lies outside each key; deleting it recovers that key, proving injection into five blocks. Exact enumeration found maximum five heavy keys and no empty common intersection. Each fixed-key outsider graph has at most four edges by the maximum-degree-two condition on four vertices, yielding n2 at most 20.
